title: China, Measures for the Labelling of AI-Generated and Synthetic Content, with GB 45438-2025

sources.title: Measures for the Labelling of AI-Generated and Synthetic Content (人工智能生成合成内容标识办法), notice of 7 March 2025, published by the Cyberspace Administration of China on 14 March 2025; Chinese text, our translation
Cyberspace Administration of China, announcement of the Measures and the mandatory national standard, 14 March 2025
GB 45438-2025, Cybersecurity technology: labelling method for content generated by artificial intelligence (in force 1 September 2025), full Chinese text as hosted by Sidley; our translation

rules.title: A visible label on generated content
rules.summary: If your generation service is offered to users in mainland China, generated text, images, audio and video carry an explicit label a person can see or hear, containing "AI" (or 人工智能) and "generated" (生成) or "synthesised" (合成). On images and video it is text at an edge or corner at least 5% of the shortest side high; audio gets a spoken notice or the Morse rhythm for "AI". Exported files keep the label unless the user asks otherwise under your agreement, and then you keep logs for six months.
rules.quote: ensure the file contains an explicit label that meets the requirements
rules.unverified: Which services must add the visible label is set by Article 17(1) of the deep synthesis provisions, which we have not re-read; the standard's Annex B lists text-to-image, music and video, cloned voices and face generation as typical. That the Measures reach only services offered to the public in mainland China is from memory.

rules.title: The AIGC metadata field in every file
rules.summary: Write an implicit label into the file's metadata: a field named AIGC with seven keys (the label value, your name or code as producer, your content number, and the reserved and distributor keys), as Annex E of GB 45438-2025 fixes. A C2PA manifest does not replace it, and it must be written before any manifest is signed. Watermarks are encouraged, not required.
rules.quote: production element information such as the attribute of the generated content, the service provider's name or code, and a content number
rules.unverified: Where the field goes in each file format is in TC260 practice guides we have not read. That the Measures reach only services offered to the public in mainland China is from memory.

rules.title: Explain the labels in your user agreement
rules.summary: Your user agreement states how and in what style content is labelled, and prompts users to read the labelling requirements.

rules.title: Do not remove or hide labels, or help others to
rules.summary: Deleting, altering, forging or hiding an AI label is prohibited, and so is supplying tools to do it.

rules.title: Declare generated content when you publish it
rules.summary: When you publish AI-generated content on a platform in China, declare it as generated and use the labelling function the platform provides. Platforms check uploads for the metadata label and mark content as generated, possibly generated or suspected generated.

changelog: 2026.10.13: first version, from /law/china as read 12 and 13 October 2026. App-store and platform duties are left out: they bind those services, not the checker's users.
